items.titleEn: Nvidia tumbles early amid questions about Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's future
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Shares of Nvidia, the chipmaker at the center of the global artificial intelligence boom, tumbled early Thursday with the tenure of CEO Jensen Huang threatened by revelations of an affair with a woman reported to be a suspected Chinese spy. The company's stock has been under pressure for weeks , both because of reporting about the affair and questions about a potential bubble in the AI sector .

items.titleEn: Nvidia CEO Huang quits after affair with suspected China spy
items.summaryEn: This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility: Jensen Huang, the leather-jacketed architect of the artificial intelligence boom, resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday after revelations of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman accused of spying for China. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a successor, the company said, ending Huang's 33 years at the helm of the global juggernaut he co-founded.

items.titleEn: Why SpaceX shares are rising on Thursday?
items.summaryEn: Buy SpaceX (SPCX). The stock is being re-rated from “rocket company” to “AI infrastructure + Starlink scale-up.” The $74B AI campus plan (Texas power-on-site + Arizona buildout) plus AI already driving >50% of revenue creates a clear growth engine, and Starship Flight 15’s tower catch/reusability milestone can further compress perceived launch-cost risk. Key Risk: Starship Flight 15 fails to catch/recover, delaying rapid reusability and making the AI infrastructure narrative look like expensive hype. Sell Nvidia (NVDA). Jensen Huang’s exit is a headline shock, and SpaceX’s AI buildout reduces the market’s urgency to keep paying up for Nvidia’s near-term dominance. If SpaceX accelerates alternative chip/data-center paths (including custom/other suppliers), NVDA’s “default AI infrastructure” premium is at risk.

items.titleEn: Jensen Huang agrees to face Congress before Thanksgiving over Chinese spy links
items.summaryEn: Buy SOXX (Semiconductor ETF). If NVDA faces China/export headwinds, the market often over-penalizes the whole AI hardware complex. But many semiconductor names are diversified across geographies and end markets; the second-order effect is that capital spending shifts toward non-China demand and toward “picks-and-shovels” components used across multiple AI platforms. Use SOXX to capture broad semiconductor upside while NVDA-specific risk is concentrated. Key Risk: A broad regulatory shock that hits the entire AI supply chain (not just NVDA) and forces widespread export restrictions across the sector. Sell NVDA. The news escalates from personal scandal to potential intelligence/export-control scrutiny tied to China links, and Congress is now in the picture with a subpoena threat. That raises the odds of tighter export enforcement, customer pullbacks, and a messy leadership transition (interim CEO) just as AI demand is priced for smooth execution. Key catalyst is the pre-Thanksgiving testimony and any follow-on actions by regulators.

items.titleEn: Trump wants Tim Cook to replace Huang at Nvidia: here's what experts think about it
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. The CEO-change headline is noise versus fundamentals: Nvidia’s core edge is product/architecture execution and customer pull in AI compute. If Tim Cook (or any strong operator) lands, the market should re-rate NVDA on smoother supply-chain scaling and fewer geopolitical bottlenecks—exactly where Cook has proven leverage (global sourcing shifts, tariff exemptions). Key Risk: A permanent leadership gap that slows next-gen chip delivery or customer adoption, not just PR—any delay in roadmap execution kills the thesis. Sell AAPL. If Tim Cook is seriously in play for Nvidia, the probability of a disruptive transition rises even if he stays as executive chairman. The market will discount Apple’s operational continuity and political/supply-chain relationships that Cook personally managed, pressuring buyback momentum and services stability.

items.titleEn: AMD stock rises as Nvidia turmoil creates an opening for chip rivals
items.summaryEn: Buy AMD. Nvidia leadership turmoil plus Intel supply delays create a real window for AMD to win share in data-center AI. The catalyst is not just sentiment: data-center revenue is already surging (up 97% YoY) and the firm expects data-center AI revenue to overtake server CPU in Q4, supported by Helios ramp through 2027. Valuation has compressed while earnings estimates rose—classic setup for multiple expansion if execution holds. Key Risk: AMD loses AI accelerator share because custom ASICs from Meta/OpenAI outcompete Instinct faster than AMD can ramp and deliver. Buy Broadcom. It’s moving with AMD, signaling the selloff is hitting Nvidia specifically, not the whole AI trade. Broadcom also has exposure to TPU/AI infrastructure demand via Alphabet and its own AI-related positioning, so it benefits if customers diversify away from Nvidia during leadership uncertainty. Upside is participation in the same supplier-switching cycle.

items.titleEn: Nvidia controversy may mean more to Alibaba stock than investors realize
items.summaryEn: Buy SOXX (Semiconductor ETF). If the US tightens AI chip flows to China, it boosts demand and pricing power for compliant, US-aligned semiconductor supply chains and accelerates domestic/ally buildouts. The market will rotate toward “winners of restriction,” not “losers of China access,” and SOXX captures that basket effect across semis benefiting from higher spend and constrained supply. Key Risk: Export controls are delayed/softened or China demand is redirected without meaningful pricing uplift, leaving semiconductor revenues broadly unchanged. Sell BABA. The Nvidia CEO controversy is being used to push tighter US oversight on AI chip exports and remote access to overseas high-end compute. That directly threatens Alibaba Cloud’s AI roadmap (Qwen training/inference capacity), raising costs and slowing model cycles versus rivals who secure compute first. The stock already fell ~7%—this is the start of a longer regulatory repricing, not a one-day headline move.

items.titleEn: Why CoreWeave, Iren shares are sliding after Nebius third-quarter earnings?
items.summaryEn: Sell CRWV. The stock is being hit by two fundamentals: (1) Nvidia leadership uncertainty threatens chip supply confidence for neoclouds, and (2) CoreWeave’s planned $4B chip-backed debt underscores the sector’s leverage risk—any funding hiccup can force slower growth or worse terms. CRWV’s rally on earnings looks fragile because the market is now repricing “growth funded by debt” as “growth funded by risk.” Key Risk: Nvidia supply and customer demand stay rock-solid and CoreWeave locks the new financing on easy terms, proving leverage is manageable. Sell IREN. It’s down harder than CRWV, signaling investors see higher refinancing/return risk in the broader neocloud complex. With Nvidia at the center of the ecosystem and IREN also tied to Nvidia as an investor, any perceived disruption hits sentiment and contract confidence. The sector already faces mounting debt; this news adds a new uncertainty layer, making IREN’s downside more immediate than any upside.

items.titleEn: All you need to know about Harvey C Jones, Nvidia's first-ever board of chair
items.summaryEn: Buy NVDA. The appointment of a long-tenured, governance-focused board chair (Harvey C. Jones) plus an interim CEO reduces the chance of a messy leadership vacuum and signals the board is tightening oversight after Jensen Huang’s resignation. NVDA’s core AI demand doesn’t change overnight; what changes is perceived governance risk, which can compress the discount on the stock. Key Risk: A real governance breakdown—new investigations find material misconduct or security/financial issues that force major operational or legal consequences. Buy SNPS. Jones’ deep ties to Synopsys (former CEO/executive chairman) make it more likely Nvidia’s board will lean on experienced EDA leadership and maintain strong relationships with key design-software vendors. If Nvidia’s governance shake-up leads to faster, more disciplined product/roadmap execution, EDA spend and tool adoption tend to hold up—benefiting SNPS.

items.titleEn: Spot gold slides to $3,864/oz after U.S. existing-home sales fall 5.5% to 3.75 million in October
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - Spot gold is falling further into the red this morning after the latest data showed the U.S. housing market performing below expectations last month. Total existing-home sales, including single-family homes, townhomes, condominiums, and co-ops, fell 5.5% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.75 million in October, the National Association of Realtors (NAR) announced on Thursday. The data was worse than expected, as the forecast of economists called for a drop to 3.85 million. September’s total was revised down to 3.97 million from 3.99 million units.
